CHAPTER 1 — जीवनसंदेशः (JIVANA-SANDESHAH: THE MESSAGE OF LIFE)

Introduction — जीवनसंदेशः कः?

The word जीवनसंदेशः is a compound of जीवनम् (life) and संदेशः (message): 'the message of life'. Sanskrit literature is not only poetry of beauty; it is also a school of living. Across the Bhagavadgita, Bhartrhari's नीतिशतकम् and the vast ocean of सुभाषित (well-said) verses, the poets of India distilled answers to the deepest practical questions: How should one act? On what should one rely? What is true wealth? What truly adorns a person? What is the place of effort? What price must a student pay for learning? In this first chapter of the NIOS Senior Secondary Sanskrit course (309) we read six celebrated public-domain verses that together form a जीवनसंदेश — a charter for living well. For each verse we study the शब्दार्थ (word meanings), the अन्वय (prose word-order), an English translation and the central message. Because this is a senior-secondary course, we then dig deeper into the grammar the verses carry: सन्धि (euphonic joining), समास (compounds), विभक्ति (case usage) and धातुरूप including the विधिलिङ् (optative) mood in which moral advice is naturally spoken.

संदेश-साहित्यम् — Why verse carries the message of life

A moral teaching in plain prose is easily forgotten; the same teaching set in metre lodges in the memory for a lifetime. That is why the Gita speaks in श्लोक and why Bhartrhari, a king turned philosopher-poet, compressed his worldly wisdom into the hundred verses of the नीतिशतकम्. Notice, as you read, how often the verbs are in the विधिलिङ् लकार (optative: उद्धरेत्, त्यजेत्, 'one should...') — Sanskrit's grammatical mood of counsel. The message of life is literally written in the grammar.

षट् श्लोकाः — Six verses with शब्दार्थ, अन्वय and message

1) आत्मोद्धारः — Lift yourself by yourself (श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता 6.5)
   उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् ।
   आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
   शब्दार्थ: उद्धरेत् = one should lift up (विधिलिङ्); आत्मना = by oneself (तृतीया); आत्मानम् = oneself (द्वितीया); न अवसादयेत् = one should not degrade / let sink; आत्मा एव = the self alone; हि = indeed; आत्मनः = of oneself (षष्ठी); बन्धुः = friend; रिपुः = enemy.
   अन्वय: (मनुष्यः) आत्मना आत्मानम् उद्धरेत्, आत्मानं न अवसादयेत् । हि आत्मा एव आत्मनः बन्धुः, आत्मा एव आत्मनः रिपुः ।
   Translation: One should raise oneself by one's own self; one should never let oneself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
   Message: आत्मनिर्भरता (self-reliance) and self-mastery. No outer helper or enemy matters as much as one's own disciplined or undisciplined mind. Life's first message: you are your own chief instrument.

2) निष्काम-कर्म — Act without craving the fruit (श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता 2.47)
   कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन ।
   मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥
   शब्दार्थ: कर्मणि = in action (सप्तमी); एव = only; अधिकारः = right, entitlement; ते = your; मा ... कदाचन = never; फलेषु = in the fruits/results (सप्तमी बहुवचन); कर्मफलहेतुः = one whose motive is the fruit of action; मा भूः = do not become; सङ्गः = attachment; मा अस्तु = let there not be; अकर्मणि = in inaction.
   अन्वय: ते अधिकारः कर्मणि एव, फलेषु कदाचन मा (अस्तु) । (त्वं) कर्मफलहेतुः मा भूः । ते अकर्मणि सङ्गः मा अस्तु ।
   Translation: Your right is to the action alone, never to its fruits. Do not become one whose motive is the fruit of action; nor let your attachment be to inaction.
   Message: कर्मयोगः. Work wholeheartedly; leave anxiety about results. Neither greed for reward nor the escape of idleness — this is the balanced ethic of work.

3) विद्याप्रशंसा — Knowledge, the hidden treasure (भर्तृहरेः नीतिशतकम्)
   विद्या नाम नरस्य रूपमधिकं प्रच्छन्नगुप्तं धनं
   विद्या भोगकरी यशःसुखकरी विद्या गुरूणां गुरुः ।
   विद्या बन्धुजनो विदेशगमने विद्या परा देवता
   विद्या राजसु पूज्यते न हि धनं विद्याविहीनः पशुः ॥
   शब्दार्थ: विद्या नाम = knowledge indeed; नरस्य = of a man (षष्ठी); रूपम् अधिकम् = beauty surpassing (outer) beauty; प्रच्छन्नगुप्तं धनम् = a hidden, well-guarded treasure; भोगकरी = giver of enjoyment; यशःसुखकरी = giver of fame and happiness; गुरूणां गुरुः = the teacher of teachers; बन्धुजनः = kinsman; विदेशगमने = when one travels abroad (सप्तमी); परा देवता = the highest deity; राजसु = among kings (सप्तमी बहुवचन); पूज्यते = is honoured (कर्मणि प्रयोग); न हि धनम् = wealth is not (so honoured); विद्याविहीनः = one devoid of learning; पशुः = a beast.
   अन्वय: विद्या नाम नरस्य अधिकं रूपम्, प्रच्छन्नगुप्तं धनम् (च अस्ति) । विद्या भोगकरी, यशःसुखकरी, गुरूणां गुरुः (च) । विदेशगमने विद्या बन्धुजनः, विद्या परा देवता । राजसु विद्या पूज्यते, न हि धनम् । विद्याविहीनः (नरः) पशुः (एव) ।
   Translation: Learning is truly a man's surpassing beauty and a hidden, guarded treasure; learning grants enjoyment, fame and happiness; learning is the teacher of teachers. In foreign lands learning is one's kinsman; learning is the highest divinity. It is learning, not wealth, that is honoured among kings. One destitute of learning is a mere beast.
   Message: विद्या is the one wealth that cannot be stolen, taxed or divided, that grows by giving. A life without learning is life at the animal level.

4) वाग्भूषणम् — Cultured speech, the only unfading ornament (भर्तृहरेः नीतिशतकम्)
   केयूराणि न भूषयन्ति पुरुषं हारा न चन्द्रोज्ज्वलाः
   न स्नानं न विलेपनं न कुसुमं नालङ्कृता मूर्धजाः ।
   वाण्येका समलङ्करोति पुरुषं या संस्कृता धार्यते
   क्षीयन्ते खलु भूषणानि सततं वाग्भूषणं भूषणम् ॥
   शब्दार्थ: केयूराणि = armlets; न भूषयन्ति = do not (truly) adorn; पुरुषम् = a person; हाराः = necklaces; चन्द्रोज्ज्वलाः = moon-bright; स्नानम् = bathing; विलेपनम् = fragrant paste; कुसुमम् = flowers; अलङ्कृताः मूर्धजाः = dressed hair; वाणी एका = speech alone; समलङ्करोति = truly adorns; या संस्कृता धार्यते = which is borne refined/cultivated; क्षीयन्ते = wear away, perish; खलु = indeed; भूषणानि = ornaments; सततम् = always; वाग्भूषणम् = the ornament of speech.
   अन्वय: केयूराणि पुरुषं न भूषयन्ति, चन्द्रोज्ज्वलाः हाराः न, स्नानं न, विलेपनं न, कुसुमं न, अलङ्कृताः मूर्धजाः न । या संस्कृता धार्यते (सा) वाणी एका पुरुषं समलङ्करोति । भूषणानि खलु क्षीयन्ते; वाग्भूषणं सततं भूषणम् ।
   Translation: Armlets do not adorn a person, nor moon-bright necklaces, nor baths, nor perfumed paste, nor flowers, nor ornamented hair. Cultivated speech alone truly adorns a person. All other ornaments wear away; the ornament of speech is the ornament forever.
   Message: Character shows in speech. Jewels fade and fashions change; refined, truthful, kind speech (संस्कृता वाणी) is the one decoration that never decays.

5) पुरुषकारः — Effort must join destiny (नीति/सुभाषितम्, हितोपदेश-परम्परा)
   यथा ह्येकेन चक्रेण न रथस्य गतिर्भवेत् ।
   एवं पुरुषकारेण विना दैवं न सिध्यति ॥
   शब्दार्थ: यथा = just as; हि = indeed; एकेन चक्रेण = with one wheel (तृतीया); रथस्य = of a chariot (षष्ठी); गतिः = motion; न भवेत् = would not be (विधिलिङ्); एवम् = so; पुरुषकारेण विना = without human effort; दैवम् = destiny, fate; न सिध्यति = does not succeed.
   अन्वय: यथा एकेन चक्रेण रथस्य गतिः न भवेत्, एवं पुरुषकारेण विना दैवं न सिध्यति ।
   Translation: Just as a chariot cannot move on one wheel, so destiny does not succeed without human effort.
   Message: Fate and effort are the two wheels of life's chariot. Waiting on luck alone is as useless as a one-wheeled chariot: उद्यम must complete दैव.

6) विद्यार्थिनः तपः — The student's choice: comfort or learning (सुभाषितम्)
   सुखार्थिनः कुतो विद्या कुतो विद्यार्थिनः सुखम् ।
   सुखार्थी वा त्यजेद्विद्यां विद्यार्थी वा त्यजेत्सुखम् ॥
   शब्दार्थ: सुखार्थिनः = for the comfort-seeker (षष्ठी); कुतः = whence, how; विद्या = learning; विद्यार्थिनः = for the seeker of learning; सुखम् = ease, comfort; वा = or; त्यजेत् = should give up (विधिलिङ्); विद्याम् = learning (द्वितीया).
   अन्वय: सुखार्थिनः विद्या कुतः? विद्यार्थिनः सुखं कुतः? सुखार्थी वा विद्यां त्यजेत्, विद्यार्थी वा सुखं त्यजेत् ।
   Translation: How can the pleasure-seeker gain learning? How can the true student expect ease? Let the pleasure-seeker give up learning, or let the student give up ease.
   Message: Excellence has a price: तपस्. Deep learning demands renouncing easy comfort — a bracing message for every senior-secondary student.

व्याकरणम् — Grammar drawn from the verses (senior-secondary level)

(A) सन्धिः. The verses are dense with sandhi; being able to perform सन्धि-विच्छेद (splitting) is essential for reading them.
  • यण्-सन्धिः (semivowel sandhi: इ/ई + vowel → य्; उ/ऊ → व्): कर्मणि + एव = कर्मण्येव; हि + आत्मनः = ह्यात्मनः; हि + एकेन = ह्येकेन; वाणी + एका = वाण्येका.
  • दीर्घ-सन्धिः (like vowels merge long): न + आत्मानम् = नात्मानम्; न + अलङ्कृताः = नालङ्कृताः; विद्या + अर्थी = विद्यार्थी (in सुखार्थी, विद्यार्थी).
  • विसर्ग-सन्धिः: अधिकारः + ते = अधिकारस्ते (visarga → स् before त्); सङ्गः + अस्तु = सङ्गोऽस्तु (अः + अ → ओ + ऽ, पूर्वरूपम् with avagraha); यशः + सुखकरी = यशःसुखकरी.
  • व्यञ्जन-सन्धिः (जश्त्वम्): उद्धरेत् + आत्मना = उद्धरेदात्मना (त् → द् before a vowel); त्यजेत् + विद्याम् = त्यजेद्विद्याम्; वाक् + भूषणम् = वाग्भूषणम् (क् → ग्).

(B) समासः. The verses use compact compounds:
  • कर्मफलहेतुः = कर्मणः फलं कर्मफलम्, तत् हेतुः यस्य सः — a बहुव्रीहि built on a षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष: 'one whose motive is the fruit of action'.
  • विद्याविहीनः = विद्यया विहीनः — तृतीया-तत्पुरुषः, 'devoid of learning'.
  • वाग्भूषणम् = वाचः भूषणम् — षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः, 'the ornament of speech'.
  • सुखार्थी / विद्यार्थी = सुखम् / विद्याम् अर्थयते इति — one who seeks comfort / learning.
  • चन्द्रोज्ज्वलाः = चन्द्रः इव उज्ज्वलाः — bright like the moon (उपमान compound).
  • पुरुषकारः = पुरुषस्य कारः — human effort; विदेशगमनम् = विदेशं गमनम् — going abroad.

(C) विभक्तिः in action: कर्मणि, फलेषु, अकर्मणि, विदेशगमने, राजसु are सप्तमी (locative) — 'in/among'; आत्मना and एकेन चक्रेण are तृतीया (instrumental) — 'by/with'; आत्मनः, नरस्य, रथस्य, गुरूणाम्, सुखार्थिनः are षष्ठी (genitive) — 'of/for'; आत्मानम्, पुरुषम्, विद्याम् are द्वितीया (accusative) objects. Note पुरुषकारेण विना: विना governs तृतीया here.

(D) धातुरूपम् and कृदन्तम्.
  • विधिलिङ् लकारः (optative, 'should'): उद्धरेत्, अवसादयेत् (णिच्), भवेत्, त्यजेत् — the mood of moral counsel.
  • लट् लकारः (present): भूषयन्ति, समलङ्करोति, सिध्यति, क्षीयन्ते.
  • कर्मणि प्रयोगः (passive): पूज्यते 'is honoured', धार्यते 'is borne/maintained'.
  • आज्ञा/निषेधः with मा: मा भूः, मा अस्तु — prohibition uses मा (not न) with लुङ्/लोट् forms.
  • कृदन्ताः (participles in क्त): प्रच्छन्न (प्र+छद्), गुप्त (गुप्), संस्कृता (सम्+कृ), अलङ्कृताः (अलम्+कृ), विहीनः (वि+हा) — past passive participles used adjectivally.

सारांशः (Summary)

The six verses of this chapter hand the student a complete जीवनसंदेश: (1) rely on and master your own self — आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुः; (2) work without craving results and without sliding into inaction — कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते; (3) treasure learning above all wealth — विद्याविहीनः पशुः; (4) let refined speech be your ornament — वाग्भूषणं भूषणम्; (5) yoke effort to destiny like the two wheels of a chariot — पुरुषकारेण विना दैवं न सिध्यति; and (6) accept the student's austerity, for comfort and deep learning cannot be held in the same hand — विद्यार्थी वा त्यजेत्सुखम्. Grammatically, you practised यण्, दीर्घ, विसर्ग and व्यञ्जन sandhis with सन्धि-विच्छेद, identified तत्पुरुष and बहुव्रीहि compounds, traced विभक्ति usage, and met the विधिलिङ् (optative) as the natural mood of advice along with कर्मणि प्रयोग and क्त-कृदन्त forms. Recite these verses until they are yours: their grammar will sharpen your Sanskrit, and their message will steady your life.

topics.name: जीवनसंदेशः — Introduction: The Message of Life
topics.description: The meaning of जीवनसंदेशः (जीवनम् + संदेशः, 'the message of life'); how Sanskrit verse literature — Gita, नीतिशतकम् and subhashitas — serves as a school of living, and why metre makes moral teaching memorable.

topics.name: Selected Verses and their Sources
topics.description: The six public-domain verses of the chapter and their sources: two from the Bhagavadgita (6.5 and 2.47), two from Bhartrhari's नीतिशतकम् (विद्या नाम..., केयूराणि न भूषयन्ति...), and two niti subhashitas (यथा ह्येकेन चक्रेण..., सुखार्थिनः कुतो विद्या...).

topics.name: शब्दार्थ and अन्वय — Word Meanings and Prose Order
topics.description: Word-by-word शब्दार्थ of each verse and the skill of अन्वय — rearranging verse into natural prose order — plus translation of the verses into clear English.

topics.name: Life-Messages and their Application
topics.description: The six life-messages — self-reliance, desireless action, the supremacy of learning, speech as the lasting ornament, effort completing destiny, and the student's austerity — analysed and applied to modern situations.

topics.name: सन्धि and समास from the Verses
topics.description: Senior-secondary sandhi work (यण्, दीर्घ, विसर्ग, व्यञ्जन sandhis with सन्धि-विच्छेद of forms like कर्मण्येव, सङ्गोऽस्तु, वाग्भूषणम्) and compound analysis (कर्मफलहेतुः, विद्याविहीनः, वाग्भूषणम्, सुखार्थी) with समास-विग्रह.

topics.name: धातुरूप and कृदन्त from the Verses
topics.description: Verb forms in the verses: विधिलिङ् (optative) as the mood of counsel (उद्धरेत्, त्यजेत्, भवेत्), लट् forms, कर्मणि प्रयोग (पूज्यते, धार्यते), prohibition with मा, and क्त-कृदन्त participles (गुप्त, संस्कृता, विहीनः).

learning_outcomes.description: Give the शब्दार्थ of words from the verses and construct or complete the अन्वय (prose order) of a given verse.
Analyse the life-message of each verse — self-reliance, निष्काम कर्म, the value of विद्या, cultured speech, effort with destiny, the student's austerity — and relate it to modern situations.

chapter_summary.title: जीवनसंदेशः (Jivana-Sandeshah) — Chapter Summary
chapter_summary.intro: This NIOS Senior Secondary Sanskrit (309) summary covers Chapter 1: six celebrated verses from the Bhagavadgita, Bhartrhari's नीतिशतकम् and the subhashita tradition that together deliver a 'message of life' — self-reliance, desireless action, the supremacy of learning, cultured speech, effort joined to destiny, and the student's austerity — along with the sandhi, samasa and verb-form grammar the verses carry.

details: भर्तृहरेः नीतिशतकम् (विद्या नाम..., केयूराणि न भूषयन्ति...)
नीति-सुभाषिते (यथा ह्येकेन चक्रेण..., सुखार्थिनः कुतो विद्या...)

पुरुषकारः + दैवम् — the chariot's two wheels

details: यण्: कर्मणि + एव = कर्मण्येव; वाणी + एका = वाण्येका

निषेधः with मा: मा भूः, मा अस्तु

sections.heading: What जीवनसंदेशः means and why it is taught in verse
bullets: जीवनसंदेशः = जीवनम् (life) + संदेशः (message): the guidance Sanskrit literature offers on how to live well.
Moral teaching set in metre is memorable for life — hence the श्लोक form of the Gita and the hundred verses of Bhartrhari's नीतिशतकम्.
The advice-mood विधिलिङ् (optative: उद्धरेत्, त्यजेत् — 'one should') is the grammatical signature of counsel in these verses.

sections.heading: The Gita verses: self-reliance and desireless action
bullets: उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानम् (Gita 6.5): raise yourself by your own self; never let yourself sink — the self alone is one's friend and one's enemy.
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते (Gita 2.47): your right is to action alone, never to its fruits; be neither fruit-driven (कर्मफलहेतुः) nor attached to inaction (अकर्मणि).
Together they teach कर्मयोग: disciplined, wholehearted work with an even mind about outcomes.

sections.heading: Bhartrhari's verses: learning and speech
bullets: विद्या नाम नरस्य रूपमधिकम्: learning is hidden treasure, giver of enjoyment and fame, teacher of teachers, kinsman abroad, highest deity — honoured among kings above wealth; विद्याविहीनः पशुः.
केयूराणि न भूषयन्ति पुरुषम्: armlets, necklaces, baths, perfumes, flowers and dressed hair do not truly adorn; only cultivated speech (संस्कृता वाणी) does.
क्षीयन्ते खलु भूषणानि: physical ornaments wear away; वाग्भूषणं सततं भूषणम् — the ornament of speech never fades.

sections.heading: The niti verses: effort and the student's price
bullets: यथा ह्येकेन चक्रेण: as a chariot cannot move on one wheel, दैव (destiny) does not succeed without पुरुषकार (human effort).
सुखार्थिनः कुतो विद्या: the comfort-seeker cannot gain learning, nor the true student expect ease — one of the two must be given up (त्यजेत्).
Both verses use विधिलिङ् forms (भवेत्, त्यजेत्) to frame their counsel as 'should', not command.

sections.heading: Grammar from the verses
bullets: सन्धि-विच्छेद: कर्मण्येव = कर्मणि + एव (यण्); नात्मानम् = न + आत्मानम् (दीर्घ); सङ्गोऽस्तु = सङ्गः + अस्तु (विसर्ग, पूर्वरूप); उद्धरेदात्मना = उद्धरेत् + आत्मना (जश्त्व); वाग्भूषणम् = वाक् + भूषणम्.
समास: कर्मफलहेतुः (बहुव्रीहि), विद्याविहीनः (तृतीया-तत्पुरुष), वाग्भूषणम् (षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष), सुखार्थी/विद्यार्थी (seeker compounds), चन्द्रोज्ज्वलाः (उपमान).
विभक्ति: सप्तमी in कर्मणि, फलेषु, राजसु, विदेशगमने; तृतीया in आत्मना, एकेन चक्रेण; षष्ठी in आत्मनः, गुरूणाम्, रथस्य.
धातुरूप/कृदन्त: विधिलिङ् उद्धरेत्/त्यजेत्/भवेत्; कर्मणि प्रयोग पूज्यते/धार्यते; निषेध with मा (मा भूः); क्त participles प्रच्छन्न, गुप्त, संस्कृता, अलङ्कृताः, विहीनः.

key_takeaways: You are your own chief friend and enemy: आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः — lift yourself by yourself.
Work is your right, results are not: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन — avoid both fruit-craving and inaction.
Learning outranks wealth everywhere, even among kings: विद्या राजसु पूज्यते न हि धनम्; विद्याविहीनः पशुः.
Refined speech is the only ornament that never wears out: वाग्भूषणं भूषणम्.
Destiny needs effort as a chariot needs both wheels: पुरुषकारेण विना दैवं न सिध्यति.
Deep learning and easy comfort cannot be held together: विद्यार्थी वा त्यजेत्सुखम्.
The विधिलिङ् (optative) is the grammar of counsel, and सन्धि-विच्छेद, समास-विग्रह and कृदन्त analysis unlock the verses' compressed style.

glossary.definition: The 'message of life' (जीवनम् + संदेशः): guidance on right living distilled in Sanskrit verses.
Bhartrhari's 'century of verses on right conduct' — a hundred niti verses on wisdom, character and worldly life.
The natural prose word-order into which a verse is rearranged so its syntax and meaning become clear.
Action performed without craving its fruit — the ethic of Gita 2.47, कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते.
One whose motive is the fruit of action — a बहुव्रीहि compound the Gita warns us not to become.
Human effort or exertion; paired with दैव (destiny) as the two wheels of life's chariot.
Destiny or fate; in the niti view it bears fruit only when joined with पुरुषकार, human effort.
The 'ornament of speech' (वाक् + भूषणम्, षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष): cultivated speech as the one unfading decoration.
One devoid of learning (विद्यया विहीनः, तृतीया-तत्पुरुष); Bhartrhari calls such a person a पशु (beast).
The optative mood ('one should...'), e.g. उद्धरेत्, त्यजेत्, भवेत् — Sanskrit's mood of advice and counsel.
The passive construction, e.g. पूज्यते 'is honoured', धार्यते 'is borne', where the object becomes the grammatical subject.
The past passive participle in -त/-ित, e.g. गुप्त, संस्कृता, अलङ्कृताः, विहीनः, used adjectivally in the verses.
Sandhi in which इ/ई and उ/ऊ become य् and व् before unlike vowels, e.g. कर्मणि + एव = कर्मण्येव.
Splitting a joined form back into its parts, e.g. सङ्गोऽस्तु = सङ्गः + अस्तु; नात्मानम् = न + आत्मानम्.
Austerity or disciplined self-denial; the price of deep learning in सुखार्थिनः कुतो विद्या.

worksheet.title: Worksheet — जीवनसंदेशः (NIOS Senior Secondary Sanskrit 309, Chapter 1)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit in Devanagari and explanations in English. Quote from the verses of the lesson wherever asked, and show सन्धि-विच्छेद and समास-विग्रह step by step.

questions.question: Name the source of each verse: (a) उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानम्... (b) विद्या नाम नरस्य रूपमधिकम्...
questions.explanation: Two of the chapter's verses are from the Gita and two from the Nitishataka.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English meaning) of: उद्धरेत्, रिपुः, पुरुषकारः, त्यजेत्.
questions.answer: उद्धरेत् = one should lift up/raise; रिपुः = enemy; पुरुषकारः = human effort; त्यजेत् = one should give up/abandon.
questions.explanation: Core vocabulary from verses 1, 5 and 6.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद and name the sandhi: (a) कर्मण्येव (b) नात्मानम् (c) सङ्गोऽस्तु.
questions.answer: (a) कर्मण्येव = कर्मणि + एव — यण्-सन्धिः (इ + ए → ये). (b) नात्मानम् = न + आत्मानम् — दीर्घ-सन्धिः (अ + आ = आ). (c) सङ्गोऽस्तु = सङ्गः + अस्तु — विसर्ग-सन्धिः (अः + अ → ओ + ऽ, पूर्वरूपम्).
questions.explanation: Three different sandhi types occur within a single Gita verse (2.47) and 6.5.

questions.question: Give the समास-विग्रह and name the समास: (a) वाग्भूषणम् (b) विद्याविहीनः.
questions.answer: (a) वाग्भूषणम् = वाचः भूषणम् — षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः ('ornament of speech'). (b) विद्याविहीनः = विद्यया विहीनः — तृतीया-तत्पुरुषः ('devoid of learning').
questions.explanation: Both are tatpurusha compounds from Bhartrhari's verses; note the जश्त्व sandhi वाक् → वाग् in the first.

questions.question: State the विभक्ति and its role: फलेषु, आत्मना, गुरूणाम्.
questions.answer: फलेषु = सप्तमी बहुवचन (locative plural), 'in the fruits/results'. आत्मना = तृतीया एकवचन (instrumental), 'by one's own self'. गुरूणाम् = षष्ठी बहुवचन (genitive plural), 'of the teachers'.
questions.explanation: सप्तमी marks the sphere, तृतीया the instrument, षष्ठी the relation.

questions.question: Write the अन्वय (prose order) of: यथा ह्येकेन चक्रेण न रथस्य गतिर्भवेत् । एवं पुरुषकारेण विना दैवं न सिध्यति ॥ and translate it.
questions.answer: अन्वय: यथा एकेन चक्रेण रथस्य गतिः न भवेत्, एवं पुरुषकारेण विना दैवं न सिध्यति । Translation: Just as a chariot cannot move on one wheel, so destiny does not succeed without human effort.
questions.explanation: The verse's compressed order is opened into subject-object-verb prose; हि is an emphatic particle left untranslated or rendered 'indeed'.

questions.question: Why does Bhartrhari call the person without learning a पशु (beast)? Answer with reference to the verse विद्या नाम नरस्य रूपमधिकम्.
questions.answer: In the verse, विद्या is everything that raises human life above mere existence: surpassing beauty, hidden treasure, giver of enjoyment and fame, teacher of teachers, kinsman abroad, highest deity, and the one thing honoured among kings above wealth. A person without learning (विद्याविहीनः) possesses none of these distinctly human excellences — he merely eats, sleeps and fears like an animal — so Bhartrhari says he is a पशु in human form.
questions.explanation: The insult is logical, not rhetorical: strip away every gift the verse attributes to विद्या and only animal life remains.

questions.question: Identify the लकार/construction of each form and translate: उद्धरेत्, पूज्यते, मा भूः.
questions.answer: उद्धरेत् = विधिलिङ् लकार (optative), 'one should lift up'. पूज्यते = लट् लकार, कर्मणि प्रयोग (present passive), 'is honoured'. मा भूः = prohibition (निषेध) with मा, 'do not become'.
questions.explanation: The optative carries counsel, the passive shifts focus to विद्या as the honoured one, and मा (never न) forms prohibitions.

questions.question: Explain the teaching of कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन (Gita 2.47) in your own words, covering both prohibitions in the second line, and show how a Class 12 student preparing for board examinations can practise this teaching.
questions.answer: The verse gives one right and two prohibitions. The right: your अधिकार (entitlement) extends to the action itself — the effort, the discipline, the doing — and never to its fruits (फलेषु कदाचन मा). First prohibition: मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूः — do not become a person whose sole motive for acting is the reward; such a person works anxiously, cuts corners, and collapses when results disappoint. Second prohibition: मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि — do not, on hearing that fruits are not yours, swing to the other extreme and become attached to inaction; renouncing results is not renouncing work. For a board-exam student this means: plan and study sincerely every day (the action is fully in your control), but do not study with the mark-sheet dangling before your eyes — anxiety about the result steals the very concentration that produces it. Equally, do not use 'results are not in my hands' as an excuse to stop studying. Work steadily, review honestly, and let the marks take care of themselves: that is निष्काम कर्म in a student's life.
questions.explanation: Full marks require: the right to action, the ban on fruit-motivation, the ban on inaction, and a concrete student application.

questions.question: क्षीयन्ते खलु भूषणानि सततं वाग्भूषणं भूषणम् — translate the full verse केयूराणि न भूषयन्ति... and discuss why the poet ranks cultivated speech above every physical ornament. Compose one Sanskrit sentence of your own in praise of good speech.
questions.answer: Translation: Armlets do not adorn a person, nor moon-bright necklaces, nor bathing, nor perfumed paste, nor flowers, nor ornamented hair; cultivated speech alone truly adorns a person. Ornaments indeed wear away; the ornament of speech is the ornament forever. Discussion: physical ornaments are external, borrowed and perishable — they decorate the body without changing the person, and क्षीयन्ते, they wear out, go out of fashion, or are removed each night. Speech, by contrast, is the direct expression of mind and character; a person of refined, truthful, kind speech (संस्कृता वाणी) is adorned in every company, at every age, even in poverty, and this adornment grows with use instead of wearing away. The poet therefore calls वाग्भूषण the only सततं भूषणम् — the permanent ornament. Own sentence (example): संस्कृता वाणी एव मनुष्यस्य सत्यम् आभूषणम् अस्ति । (Cultivated speech alone is a person's true ornament.)
questions.explanation: Any grammatically sound Sanskrit sentence in praise of speech earns the composition mark.

questions.question: The word जीवनसंदेशः is formed from जीवनम् + ____.
questions.explanation: जीवनम् (life) + संदेशः (message) = 'the message of life'.

questions.question: Why is moral teaching in Sanskrit traditionally set in verse (श्लोक) rather than prose?
options: Verse is memorable and lodges the teaching in memory
Prose was forbidden in ancient India
Verses are easier to write than prose
Only kings were allowed to read prose
questions.answer: Verse is memorable and lodges the teaching in memory
questions.explanation: Metre makes wisdom easy to memorise and recite for a lifetime.

questions.question: Which grammatical mood is called the 'mood of counsel' because moral advice like उद्धरेत् and त्यजेत् is spoken in it?
questions.explanation: विधिलिङ् expresses 'one should...', the natural voice of counsel.

questions.question: भर्तृहरिः is remembered in tradition as
options: a king turned philosopher-poet who wrote the नीतिशतकम्
a grammarian who wrote the अष्टाध्यायी
a physician who wrote on Ayurveda
questions.answer: a king turned philosopher-poet who wrote the नीतिशतकम्
questions.explanation: Bhartrhari, traditionally a king who renounced, composed the shataka trilogy including the नीतिशतकम्.

questions.question: नीतिशतकम् literally means
options: a century (hundred) of verses on right conduct
a story of a hundred kings
questions.answer: a century (hundred) of verses on right conduct
questions.explanation: नीति (right conduct/worldly wisdom) + शतकम् (a set of one hundred verses).

questions.question: The chapter says 'the message of life is literally written in the grammar' of the verses. This refers to
options: the repeated use of optative (विधिलिङ्) verbs that voice counsel
the use of long compounds in every verse
the absence of any verbs in the verses
the use of Vedic accents in the text
questions.answer: the repeated use of optative (विधिलिङ्) verbs that voice counsel
questions.explanation: Forms like उद्धरेत्, त्यजेत्, भवेत् grammatically encode 'one should' — advice built into the verb.

questions.question: The verse उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् is taken from
questions.explanation: It is Bhagavadgita 6.5, the verse of self-upliftment.

questions.question: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन occurs in the Bhagavadgita in adhyaya
questions.explanation: Gita 2.47 is the celebrated verse of desireless action.

questions.question: विद्या नाम नरस्य रूपमधिकं प्रच्छन्नगुप्तं धनम् is a verse of
questions.explanation: It is Bhartrhari's famous praise of learning from the Nitishataka.

questions.question: Which verse of the chapter ends with the words वाग्भूषणं भूषणम्?
questions.explanation: Bhartrhari's verse on ornaments concludes that speech is the everlasting ornament.

questions.question: The simile of the one-wheeled chariot (एकेन चक्रेण) is used to teach that
options: destiny does not succeed without human effort
the self is its own enemy
questions.answer: destiny does not succeed without human effort
questions.explanation: यथा ह्येकेन चक्रेण... एवं पुरुषकारेण विना दैवं न सिध्यति.

questions.question: सुखार्थिनः कुतो विद्या कुतो विद्यार्थिनः सुखम् — the second line of this subhashita says
options: सुखार्थी वा त्यजेद्विद्यां विद्यार्थी वा त्यजेत्सुखम्
क्षीयन्ते खलु भूषणानि सततं वाग्भूषणं भूषणम्
questions.answer: सुखार्थी वा त्यजेद्विद्यां विद्यार्थी वा त्यजेत्सुखम्
questions.explanation: The verse concludes: let the comfort-seeker give up learning, or the student give up comfort.

questions.question: Which pair of verses in this chapter comes from the Bhagavadgita?
options: विद्या नाम... and केयूराणि न भूषयन्ति...
यथा ह्येकेन चक्रेण... and सुखार्थिनः कुतो विद्या...
केयूराणि न भूषयन्ति... and यथा ह्येकेन चक्रेण...
questions.explanation: Gita 6.5 and Gita 2.47; the other four are from Bhartrhari and the subhashita tradition.

questions.question: In the verse विद्या नाम..., which of the following is NOT one of the epithets given to विद्या?
questions.explanation: The verse says विद्या बन्धुजनो विदेशगमने — learning is a KINSMAN abroad, not an enemy.

questions.question: Match the opening words to the theme: (i) उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानम् (ii) केयूराणि न भूषयन्ति (iii) यथा ह्येकेन चक्रेण — themes: (a) effort and destiny (b) self-reliance (c) speech as ornament.
questions.explanation: Self-upliftment (Gita 6.5), speech as ornament (Bhartrhari), effort completing destiny (niti verse).

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: In उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानम्, the word रिपुः means
questions.explanation: आत्मैव रिपुरात्मनः — the self alone is the enemy of the self.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: कदाचन in मा फलेषु कदाचन means
questions.explanation: मा ... कदाचन together mean 'never at any time'.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: In Bhartrhari's verse, केयूराणि means
questions.explanation: केयूरम् is an armlet worn on the upper arm; the plural is केयूराणि.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: क्षीयन्ते in क्षीयन्ते खलु भूषणानि means
questions.explanation: From the root क्षि 'to decay': ornaments wear away, but the ornament of speech does not.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: In यथा ह्येकेन चक्रेण..., the word दैवम् means
questions.explanation: दैवम् (from देव) here means fate/destiny, contrasted with पुरुषकार, human effort.

questions.question: In the अन्वय of उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानम्, the correct prose order of the first line is
options: (मनुष्यः) आत्मना आत्मानम् उद्धरेत्, आत्मानं न अवसादयेत्
आत्मानम् आत्मना (मनुष्यः) न उद्धरेत्, अवसादयेत् आत्मानम्
questions.answer: (मनुष्यः) आत्मना आत्मानम् उद्धरेत्, आत्मानं न अवसादयेत्
questions.explanation: Subject (understood मनुष्यः), instrument आत्मना, object आत्मानम्, verbs उद्धरेत् / न अवसादयेत्.

questions.question: यशःसुखकरी, said of विद्या, means
questions.explanation: यशः (fame) + सुख (happiness) + करी (feminine 'maker/giver').

questions.question: In the phrase या संस्कृता धार्यते, the relative या refers to
questions.explanation: वाण्येका समलङ्करोति पुरुषं या संस्कृता धार्यते — the speech which is borne refined.

questions.question: In सुखार्थिनः कुतो विद्या, the word कुतः expresses
questions.explanation: कुतः ('from where?') is rhetorical: for the pleasure-seeker learning is impossible.

questions.question: In मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूः, the word भूः is
options: a verb form, 'become' (with मा: 'do not become')
questions.answer: a verb form, 'become' (with मा: 'do not become')
questions.explanation: मा भूः is a prohibition: 'do not become (one whose motive is the fruit)'; भूः here is not the noun 'earth'.

questions.question: The central message of Gita 6.5 (उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानम्) is
options: self-reliance: lift yourself by your own self
silence: speak as little as possible
questions.answer: self-reliance: lift yourself by your own self
questions.explanation: The verse teaches आत्मनिर्भरता — the self is one's own chief friend and enemy.

questions.question: According to Gita 2.47, a person's अधिकार (rightful claim) extends to
options: the action alone, not its fruits
the fruits alone, not the action
questions.answer: the action alone, not its fruits
questions.explanation: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन — your right is to the work, never to the results.

questions.question: मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि warns against
options: attachment to inaction (using detachment as an excuse for idleness)
questions.answer: attachment to inaction (using detachment as an excuse for idleness)
questions.explanation: Renouncing the fruit must not slide into renouncing work itself.

questions.question: Why does Bhartrhari call विद्या a प्रच्छन्नगुप्तं धनम् (hidden, guarded treasure)?
options: It stays invisibly with its owner and cannot be stolen or divided
It must be kept secret from teachers
It is buried underground for safety
It is written in coded language
questions.answer: It stays invisibly with its owner and cannot be stolen or divided
questions.explanation: Unlike money, learning is carried invisibly and no thief or tax can take it.

questions.question: In the chariot simile, the 'two wheels' on which life's chariot moves are
questions.explanation: Destiny without effort is a one-wheeled chariot — it cannot move.

questions.question: A student who says 'my stars are bad, so studying is useless' is directly refuted by which verse?
options: यथा ह्येकेन चक्रेण न रथस्य गतिर्भवेत्...
questions.answer: यथा ह्येकेन चक्रेण न रथस्य गतिर्भवेत्...
questions.explanation: The verse insists destiny fructifies only when joined with human effort.

questions.question: An athlete who trains sincerely but obsesses so much over the medal that anxiety ruins her performance is failing which teaching?
questions.explanation: Craving the fruit (the medal) rather than focusing on the action is exactly what Gita 2.47 forbids.

questions.question: Bhartrhari ranks वाणी (speech) above jewels because
options: speech expresses character and grows with use while jewels perish
speech is cheaper to acquire than jewels
speech can be sold for a higher price
questions.answer: speech expresses character and grows with use while jewels perish
questions.explanation: क्षीयन्ते खलु भूषणानि — ornaments decay; cultivated speech adorns forever because it is the person, not a covering.

questions.question: The verses सुखार्थिनः कुतो विद्या and उद्यमेन हि सिध्यन्ति (studied in earlier classes) share which common conviction?
options: Achievement demands renouncing ease and exerting effort
Wealth is the highest goal of life
questions.answer: Achievement demands renouncing ease and exerting effort
questions.explanation: Both verses reject comfort-seeking and idle wishing in favour of disciplined exertion.

questions.question: सन्धि-विच्छेद of नात्मानम् is
questions.explanation: अ + आ merge into आ by दीर्घ-सन्धि.

questions.question: कर्मण्येव = कर्मणि + एव is an example of
questions.explanation: The इ of कर्मणि becomes य् before the unlike vowel ए — yan sandhi.

questions.question: सन्धि-विच्छेद of सङ्गोऽस्तु is
questions.explanation: अः + अ → ओ + ऽ (avagraha) by visarga sandhi with पूर्वरूप.

questions.question: The sign ऽ (अवग्रहः) written in सङ्गोऽस्तु indicates
options: the elision of an initial अ after ओ/ए
the end of a verse quarter
questions.answer: the elision of an initial अ after ओ/ए
questions.explanation: The avagraha marks the lost अ of अस्तु after सङ्गो.

questions.question: वाण्येका should be split as
questions.explanation: ई + ए → ये by यण्-सन्धि: the ई of वाणी becomes य्.

questions.question: उद्धरेदात्मना = उद्धरेत् + आत्मना shows which change?
questions.explanation: A final voiceless त् becomes voiced द् before a vowel — jashtva consonant sandhi.

questions.question: वाग्भूषणम् is formed from वाक् + भूषणम् by
options: क् → ग् (जश्त्वम्) before the voiced भ्
questions.answer: क् → ग् (जश्त्वम्) before the voiced भ्
questions.explanation: The voiceless क् voices to ग् before the voiced consonant भ्.

questions.question: अधिकारस्ते = अधिकारः + ते illustrates
questions.explanation: Visarga becomes स् before the dental त्: अधिकारस्ते.

questions.question: त्यजेद्विद्याम् should be split as
questions.explanation: The original pada is त्यजेत्; its त् voices to द् before the voiced व् of विद्याम्.

questions.question: Which of the following is a यण्-सन्धि form from the verses?
questions.explanation: The इ of हि becomes य् before आ — yan sandhi; the others are dirgha, visarga and jashtva.

questions.question: In सुखार्थी the join सुख + अर्थी shows the same sandhi as in
questions.explanation: Both are दीर्घ-सन्धि: like vowels अ/आ merging into long आ.

questions.question: The विग्रह of वाग्भूषणम् is
questions.explanation: 'Ornament OF speech' — genitive (षष्ठी) relation, hence षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष.

questions.question: विद्याविहीनः = विद्यया विहीनः is which समास?
questions.explanation: The first member stands in the instrumental (विद्यया 'by/of learning deprived').

questions.question: कर्मफलहेतुः in मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूः is best analysed as
options: कर्मणः फलं हेतुः यस्य सः — a बहुव्रीहि: 'one whose motive is the fruit of action'
कर्म च फलं च हेतुः च — a द्वन्द्व of three items
questions.answer: कर्मणः फलं हेतुः यस्य सः — a बहुव्रीहि: 'one whose motive is the fruit of action'
questions.explanation: The compound describes a person (Arjuna) — external reference marks a bahuvrihi built on कर्मफल.

questions.question: चन्द्रोज्ज्वलाः describing हाराः (necklaces) means
questions.explanation: चन्द्रः इव उज्ज्वलाः — an उपमान (simile) compound.

questions.question: In कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते, the word कर्मणि is in which विभक्ति?
questions.explanation: कर्मणि is the locative singular of कर्मन्: your right lies IN the action.

questions.question: आत्मना in उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानम् is
questions.explanation: आत्मना is the instrumental of आत्मन्: the self is the instrument of upliftment.

questions.question: राजसु in विद्या राजसु पूज्यते is
questions.explanation: राजसु is locative plural of राजन्: learning is honoured AMONG kings.

questions.question: In पुरुषकारेण विना ('without effort'), the indeclinable विना here governs
questions.explanation: विना may take द्वितीया, तृतीया or पञ्चमी; here पुरुषकारेण is instrumental.

questions.question: गुरूणां गुरुः ('teacher of teachers') uses which विभक्ति in गुरूणाम्?
questions.explanation: The 'of' relation: विद्या is the guru OF all gurus.

questions.question: विद्यार्थी and सुखार्थी are formed with अर्थिन् meaning
options: 'one who seeks' — a seeker of learning / of comfort
questions.answer: 'one who seeks' — a seeker of learning / of comfort
questions.explanation: अर्थिन् (from अर्थ् 'to seek/request') gives 'seeker': विद्याम् अर्थयते इति विद्यार्थी.

questions.question: Which pair correctly matches compound and type?
questions.explanation: वाचः भूषणम् (genitive relation); विद्यया विहीनः (instrumental relation).

questions.question: उद्धरेत् ('one should lift up') is in which लकार?
questions.explanation: The -एत् ending marks the optative, the mood of 'should'.

questions.question: सिध्यति in दैवं न सिध्यति is in which लकार?
questions.explanation: सिध्यति is present tense, third person singular of सिध्.

questions.question: पूज्यते in विद्या राजसु पूज्यते is
questions.explanation: The -य- suffix with atmanepada ending marks the passive: विद्या is honoured.

questions.question: धार्यते in या संस्कृता धार्यते means
questions.explanation: Passive of धृ: the refined speech IS BORNE by the person.

questions.question: In Sanskrit, prohibitions like मा भूः ('do not become') are formed with
questions.explanation: मा is the prohibitive particle; न merely negates statements.

questions.question: अवसादयेत् in नात्मानमवसादयेत् is a causative (णिच्) optative meaning
questions.explanation: सद् with अव + णिच् = अवसादय- 'cause to sink'; with न: one should not let oneself sink.

questions.question: Which of these is a क्त-कृदन्त (past passive participle) from the verses?
questions.explanation: संस्कृता 'refined' is a kta-participle qualifying वाणी; the others are a verb and an indeclinable.

questions.question: विहीनः in विद्याविहीनः is derived from
questions.explanation: The root हा 'to abandon' with वि and the क्त suffix gives विहीन 'left without'.

questions.question: भूषयन्ति (in केयूराणि न भूषयन्ति) and भवेत् (in गतिर्भवेत्) differ in that
options: भूषयन्ति is लट् plural 'they adorn'; भवेत् is विधिलिङ् singular 'would/should be'
भूषयन्ति is passive; भवेत् is causative
questions.answer: भूषयन्ति is लट् plural 'they adorn'; भवेत् is विधिलिङ् singular 'would/should be'
questions.explanation: The verses mix a present statement of fact with an optative hypothesis.

questions.question: क्षीयन्ते in क्षीयन्ते खलु भूषणानि is
questions.explanation: Third person plural of क्षि in the -य- present: the many ornaments all perish.

questions.question: Following the pattern of त्यजेत् (त्यज् + विधिलिङ्), the विधिलिङ् third-person singular of पठ् ('to read') is
questions.explanation: Root + -एत् gives the optative: पठेत् 'one should read'.

questions.question: The best English rendering of आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुः is
options: The self alone is the friend of the self
The soul has no friends at all
A friend is better than the soul
questions.answer: The self alone is the friend of the self
questions.explanation: आत्मा एव (the self alone) + आत्मनः (of the self) + बन्धुः (friend).

questions.question: Which translation best captures मा फलेषु कदाचन?
options: never (let your claim be) to the fruits
questions.answer: never (let your claim be) to the fruits
questions.explanation: मा + कदाचन is an absolute 'never'; फलेषु means 'in/to the results', not literal fruit-eating.

questions.question: विद्याविहीनः पशुः is best translated as
options: One devoid of learning is a beast
questions.answer: One devoid of learning is a beast
questions.explanation: The nominal sentence equates the unlearned person with a पशु.

questions.question: Which Sanskrit sentence correctly says 'A student should give up laziness'?
questions.explanation: Subject in प्रथमा (छात्रः), object in द्वितीया (आलस्यम्), optative verb त्यजेत्.

questions.question: For वाग्भूषणं भूषणम्, which rendering best keeps the verse's emphasis?
options: Speech is THE ornament — the only one that lasts
An ornament is a kind of speech
Ornaments should be praised in speech
Speech and ornaments are equally valuable
questions.answer: Speech is THE ornament — the only one that lasts
questions.explanation: The repetition भूषणं भूषणम् with सततम् asserts speech as the ornament par excellence.

questions.question: Which Sanskrit sentence correctly uses the chapter's vocabulary to say 'Learning is honoured everywhere'?
questions.explanation: In the passive, विद्या stands in प्रथमा with the singular passive verb पूज्यते.

questions.question: A translator renders सुखार्थिनः कुतो विद्या as 'The pleasure-seeker will fail his examinations'. This rendering is faulty because
options: it narrows the verse's universal claim about learning to one modern situation
it uses the future tense, which Sanskrit lacks
the verse is about wealth, not learning
questions.answer: it narrows the verse's universal claim about learning to one modern situation
questions.explanation: The verse states a timeless incompatibility of comfort-seeking and learning, not an exam prediction.

questions.question: To advise a friend in Sanskrit 'One should rise early' (in the counsel-mood of this chapter), the aptest sentence is
questions.explanation: Counsel takes the विधिलिङ्: उत्तिष्ठेत् 'one should rise', matching उद्धरेत्/त्यजेत्.

questions.question: जीवनसंदेशः means 'the message of life', and this chapter draws that message from the Gita, Bhartrhari and the subhashita tradition.
questions.explanation: जीवनम् + संदेशः; the chapter's six verses come from exactly these sources.

questions.question: The verse केयूराणि न भूषयन्ति पुरुषम् is taken from the Bhagavadgita.
questions.explanation: It is from Bhartrhari's नीतिशतकम्, not the Gita.

questions.question: In the verse विद्या नाम..., learning is said to be one's बन्धुजन (kinsman) when travelling abroad (विदेशगमने).
questions.explanation: विद्या बन्धुजनो विदेशगमने — in a foreign land learning serves as one's kin.

questions.question: Gita 2.47 teaches that since the fruits are not ours, it is best to give up action altogether.
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly forbids attachment to inaction: मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि.

questions.question: The सन्धि-विच्छेद of कर्मण्येव is कर्मणि + एव, an example of यण्-सन्धि.
questions.explanation: The इ of कर्मणि becomes य् before ए.

questions.question: In वाग्भूषणम्, the original क् of वाक् has changed to ग् because the following भ् is a voiced consonant.
questions.explanation: जश्त्व: a voiceless stop voices before a voiced consonant — वाक् + भूषणम् = वाग्भूषणम्.

questions.question: विद्याविहीनः is a द्वन्द्व compound meaning 'learning and loss'.
questions.explanation: It is a तृतीया-तत्पुरुष: विद्यया विहीनः, 'devoid of learning'.

questions.question: The forms उद्धरेत्, त्यजेत् and भवेत् are all in the विधिलिङ् (optative) लकार.
questions.explanation: All three carry the -एत् optative ending expressing 'should'.

questions.question: In विद्या राजसु पूज्यते, the verb पूज्यते is in the active voice (कर्तरि प्रयोग).
questions.explanation: पूज्यते is passive (कर्मणि प्रयोग): learning IS honoured among kings.

questions.question: An acceptable translation of सुखार्थी वा त्यजेद्विद्याम् is 'Let the comfort-seeker give up learning'.
questions.explanation: त्यजेत् (optative) + विद्याम् (object): the comfort-lover must renounce learning.

questions.question: Complete the verse: उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानम् ____ । (one should not let oneself sink)
questions.explanation: Gita 6.5: नात्मानमवसादयेत् — never degrade/let sink oneself.

questions.question: Complete: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा ____ कदाचन ।
questions.explanation: Gita 2.47: never let your claim rest in the fruits (फलेषु).

questions.question: Complete Bhartrhari's line: विद्या भोगकरी यशःसुखकरी विद्या ____ गुरुः ।
questions.explanation: विद्या गुरूणां गुरुः — learning is the teacher of teachers.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: The Sanskrit word for 'enemy' used in आत्मैव रिपुरात्मनः is ____.
questions.explanation: रिपुः = enemy; the self can be its own enemy.

questions.question: शब्दार्थ: In यथा ह्येकेन चक्रेण, human effort is called ____ (one word from the verse's second line).
questions.explanation: पुरुषकारेण विना — without पुरुषकार (human effort) destiny fails.

questions.question: In Bhartrhari's ornament verse, the one thing that truly adorns a person is संस्कृता ____ (refined ____).
questions.explanation: वाण्येका समलङ्करोति पुरुषम् — cultivated speech alone adorns.

questions.question: Complete the अन्वय: सुखार्थिनः विद्या कुतः? विद्यार्थिनः ____ कुतः?
questions.explanation: The parallel question: whence comfort for the seeker of learning?

questions.question: सन्धि-विच्छेद: ह्यात्मनः = हि + ____.
questions.explanation: यण्-सन्धि: the इ of हि becomes य् before आ.

questions.question: सन्धि: वाक् + भूषणम् = ____.
questions.explanation: क् voices to ग् before भ् (जश्त्व sandhi).

questions.question: सन्धि-विच्छेद: त्यजेत्सुखम् = त्यजेत् + ____.
questions.explanation: The words त्यजेत् and सुखम् are written joined in the verse.

questions.question: समास-विग्रह: वाग्भूषणम् = वाचः ____ ।
questions.explanation: 'The ornament of speech' — a षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष.

questions.question: समास-विग्रह: विद्याविहीनः = ____ विहीनः (supply the correct instrumental form).
questions.explanation: तृतीया-तत्पुरुष: विद्यया विहीनः, deprived of learning.

questions.question: विभक्ति: In कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते, the locative singular of कर्मन् appearing in the verse is ____.
questions.explanation: कर्मणि = सप्तमी एकवचन of कर्मन्, 'in action'.

questions.question: धातुरूप: The विधिलिङ् form of त्यज् used twice in सुखार्थिनः कुतो विद्या... is ____.
questions.explanation: त्यजेद्विद्यां / त्यजेत्सुखम् — 'should give up'.

questions.question: The passive (कर्मणि) verb meaning 'is honoured' in विद्या राजसु ____ is ____ (same word fills both blanks).
questions.explanation: विद्या राजसु पूज्यते — learning is honoured among kings.

questions.question: What does जीवनसंदेशः mean, and from which three streams of Sanskrit literature does this chapter draw its verses?
questions.answer: जीवनसंदेशः (जीवनम् + संदेशः) means 'the message of life' — guidance on how to live well. The chapter draws its six verses from the Bhagavadgita, Bhartrhari's नीतिशतकम्, and the anonymous niti-subhashita tradition.
questions.explanation: Definition plus the three sources.

questions.question: Why is the विधिलिङ् called the 'grammatical mood of counsel', and why does it dominate the verses of this chapter?
questions.answer: The विधिलिङ् (optative) expresses 'one should/ought to' rather than a command or a plain statement — the tone of advice. Since the chapter's verses ARE advice on living (lift yourself, give up comfort, act without craving), their key verbs — उद्धरेत्, अवसादयेत्, त्यजेत्, भवेत् — naturally stand in the विधिलिङ्.
questions.explanation: Mood meaning + link to the advisory content.

questions.question: Quote the two lines of the Gita verse on self-reliance studied in this chapter.
questions.answer: उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥ (Bhagavadgita 6.5)
questions.explanation: The verse of आत्मोद्धार, self-upliftment.

questions.question: Identify each verse's theme from its opening words: (a) विद्या नाम नरस्य रूपमधिकम् (b) सुखार्थिनः कुतो विद्या.
questions.answer: (a) The praise of learning: विद्या as surpassing beauty, hidden treasure, teacher of teachers, kinsman abroad, highest deity — while the unlearned is a पशु. (b) The student's austerity: comfort and learning cannot be had together; one of the two must be renounced.
questions.explanation: Both are anthology staples: Bhartrhari's vidya-prashamsa and the sukharthi subhashita.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: अधिकारः, सङ्गः, अकर्मणि, कदाचन.
questions.answer: अधिकारः = right/entitlement; सङ्गः = attachment; अकर्मणि = in inaction (locative); कदाचन = ever/at any time (with मा: never).
questions.explanation: All four words are from Gita 2.47.

questions.question: Write the अन्वय of: मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि, and translate it.
questions.answer: अन्वय: (त्वं) कर्मफलहेतुः मा भूः । ते अकर्मणि सङ्गः मा अस्तु । Translation: Do not become one whose motive is the fruit of action; and let there be no attachment of yours to inaction.
questions.explanation: Two prohibitions with मा, split from the sandhi-joined verse line.

questions.question: List any four of the epithets Bhartrhari gives to विद्या in विद्या नाम नरस्य रूपमधिकम्, with their meanings.
questions.answer: Any four of: अधिकं रूपम् — surpassing beauty; प्रच्छन्नगुप्तं धनम् — hidden guarded treasure; भोगकरी — giver of enjoyment; यशःसुखकरी — giver of fame and happiness; गुरूणां गुरुः — teacher of teachers; बन्धुजनः विदेशगमने — kinsman when abroad; परा देवता — the highest deity.
questions.explanation: The verse strings seven epithets before its climax विद्याविहीनः पशुः.

questions.question: In the ornament verse, list the six things the poet says do NOT truly adorn a person, in Sanskrit with English meanings.
questions.answer: केयूराणि (armlets), हाराः चन्द्रोज्ज्वलाः (moon-bright necklaces), स्नानम् (bathing), विलेपनम् (fragrant paste/unguents), कुसुमम् (flowers), अलङ्कृताः मूर्धजाः (ornamented/dressed hair).
questions.explanation: Six negations build up to वाणी एका समलङ्करोति — speech alone adorns.

questions.question: In what sense is the आत्मा both बन्धु (friend) and रिपु (enemy) according to Gita 6.5?
questions.answer: The self is a friend when it is disciplined — when the mind is mastered, it lifts the person toward every good goal. The same self is an enemy when undisciplined — a mind ruled by laziness, craving and negativity drags the person down more surely than any outer foe. Hence the verse: raise yourself by yourself, never let yourself sink.
questions.explanation: The paradox dissolves once 'self' is read as the mind in its mastered vs unmastered states.

questions.question: Explain the two dangers Gita 2.47 warns against, and why avoiding both is called the balanced ethic of work.
questions.answer: Danger one: becoming कर्मफलहेतुः — acting only for the reward, which breeds anxiety and dishonesty. Danger two: सङ्गः अकर्मणि — attachment to inaction, using 'results are not mine' as an excuse for idleness. The ethic is balanced because it steers between greed and laziness: full effort in the action, full detachment from the outcome.
questions.explanation: The verse's two मा-prohibitions mark the two ditches on either side of the road of work.

questions.question: Compare the messages of यथा ह्येकेन चक्रेण and सुखार्थिनः कुतो विद्या: what single conviction about effort do they share, and how do they differ in focus?
questions.answer: Shared conviction: nothing worthwhile comes without exertion — destiny needs पुरुषकार, and learning needs the sacrifice of comfort. Difference of focus: the chariot verse addresses fatalism (do not wait on luck; add your own wheel of effort), while the student verse addresses comfort-seeking (do not expect ease and excellence together; choose). One argues against passivity toward fate, the other against self-indulgence.
questions.explanation: Both verses attack a different excuse for not working.

questions.question: A classmate argues: 'Bhartrhari exaggerates — money, not learning, is honoured everywhere today.' Reply using the verse विद्या नाम..., conceding what is true and defending the verse's core claim.
questions.answer: Concede: wealth certainly commands attention in the market-place. But the verse's claim survives: wealth can be stolen, divided and exhausted, while विद्या is प्रच्छन्नगुप्तं धनम् — a treasure that travels invisibly with its owner, serves as kinsman in a strange land, and grows by being spent. Even today, lasting respect (राजसु पूज्यते) goes to knowledge and competence; money without learning buys attention, not honour. The unlearned rich person still lives at the level Bhartrhari calls पशु — consuming without understanding.
questions.explanation: An evaluation answer: acknowledge the objection, then argue the verse's distinction between attention and honour.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद and name the sandhi: (a) वाण्येका (b) ह्येकेन.
questions.answer: (a) वाण्येका = वाणी + एका — यण्-सन्धिः (ई → य् before ए). (b) ह्येकेन = हि + एकेन — यण्-सन्धिः (इ → य् before ए).
questions.explanation: Both show a final इ/ई becoming य् before an unlike vowel.

questions.question: Split into words, naming each sandhi: मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि.
questions.answer: मा + कर्मफलहेतुः + भूः + मा + ते + सङ्गः + अस्तु + अकर्मणि. Sandhis: हेतुः + भूः → हेतुर्भूः and भूः + मा → भूर्मा (विसर्ग → र् before voiced sounds); सङ्गः + अस्तु → सङ्गोऽस्तु (विसर्ग-सन्धि with पूर्वरूप, avagraha); अस्तु + अकर्मणि → अस्त्वकर्मणि (यण्: उ → व् before अ).
questions.explanation: One Gita line packs visarga-to-r, purvarupa and yan sandhis together.

questions.question: From the verses, give one example each of दीर्घ-सन्धि, यण्-सन्धि, विसर्ग-सन्धि and व्यञ्जन-सन्धि (जश्त्व), with the split.
questions.answer: दीर्घ: नात्मानम् = न + आत्मानम् (अ + आ = आ). यण्: कर्मण्येव = कर्मणि + एव (इ → य्). विसर्ग: अधिकारस्ते = अधिकारः + ते (ः → स्) or सङ्गोऽस्तु = सङ्गः + अस्तु. व्यञ्जन/जश्त्व: उद्धरेदात्मना = उद्धरेत् + आत्मना (त् → द्) or वाग्भूषणम् = वाक् + भूषणम् (क् → ग्).
questions.explanation: The four sandhi families of the chapter, one instance each.

questions.question: Give the समास-विग्रह of सुखार्थी and विद्यार्थी and explain the shared formation.
questions.answer: सुखार्थी = सुखम् अर्थयते इति (one who seeks comfort); विद्यार्थी = विद्याम् अर्थयते इति (one who seeks learning). Both attach अर्थिन् 'seeker' to the thing sought, joined by दीर्घ-सन्धि (सुख + अर्थी, विद्या + अर्थी).
questions.explanation: Parallel 'seeker' compounds that structure the whole verse.

questions.question: State the विभक्ति, वचन and role of: विदेशगमने, एकेन चक्रेण, रथस्य.
questions.answer: विदेशगमने = सप्तमी एकवचन, 'at (the time of) going abroad' — locative of occasion. एकेन चक्रेण = तृतीया एकवचन (adjective + noun), 'with one wheel' — instrument. रथस्य = षष्ठी एकवचन, 'of the chariot' — possession/relation (रथस्य गतिः, the chariot's motion).
questions.explanation: Locative of occasion, instrumental of means, genitive of relation.

questions.question: Why is कर्मफलहेतुः classified as a बहुव्रीहि and not a simple तत्पुरुष? Give its full विग्रह.
questions.answer: विग्रह: कर्मणः फलं कर्मफलम् (a षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष within), then कर्मफलं हेतुः यस्य सः कर्मफलहेतुः — 'he WHOSE motive is the fruit of action'. Because the compound as a whole refers to a person outside itself (Arjuna, the agent), not to the fruit or the motive themselves, it is a बहुव्रीहि; a tatpurusha would denote the thing itself (e.g. 'the motive of the fruit').
questions.explanation: External reference (अन्यपदार्थप्रधानता) is the test for bahuvrihi.

questions.question: Pick out all the विधिलिङ् forms occurring in the six verses of the chapter and give the root of each.
questions.answer: उद्धरेत् (उद् + हृ, 'should lift up'); अवसादयेत् (अव + सद् in the causative, 'should [not] let sink'); भवेत् (भू, 'would be'); त्यजेत् (त्यज्, 'should give up' — used twice, त्यजेद्विद्यां / त्यजेत्सुखम्).
questions.explanation: Four optative forms carry the chapter's counsel.

questions.question: Identify the formation of each participle and the word it qualifies: प्रच्छन्न, संस्कृता, अलङ्कृताः.
questions.answer: प्रच्छन्न = प्र + छद् + क्त, 'hidden', qualifying धनम् (in प्रच्छन्नगुप्तं धनम्). संस्कृता = सम् + कृ + क्त (feminine), 'refined/cultivated', qualifying वाणी. अलङ्कृताः = अलम् + कृ + क्त (masculine plural), 'ornamented/dressed', qualifying मूर्धजाः (hair).
questions.explanation: All three are क्त past passive participles used adjectivally, agreeing in gender and number.

questions.question: Translate into idiomatic English: विद्या बन्धुजनो विदेशगमने विद्या परा देवता । विद्या राजसु पूज्यते न हि धनम् ॥
questions.answer: In foreign lands learning is one's own kin; learning is the highest divinity. It is learning, not wealth, that is honoured among kings.
questions.explanation: बन्धुजनः = kinsman; note the contrastive न हि धनम् — 'and NOT wealth'.

questions.question: Compose two Sanskrit sentences in the विधिलिङ् giving advice to a fellow student, using vocabulary from this chapter. Provide English translations.
questions.answer: Example: 1. छात्रः आलस्यं त्यजेत्, विद्यां च सेवेत । (A student should give up laziness and devote himself to learning.) 2. मनुष्यः आत्मना आत्मानम् उद्धरेत् । (A person should lift himself up by his own self.) Any two grammatically correct optative sentences using chapter vocabulary are acceptable.
questions.explanation: Tests active use of the counsel-mood with chapter words like त्यजेत्, उद्धरेत्, विद्या, आलस्यम्.

questions.question: 'Sanskrit literature is not only poetry of beauty; it is also a school of living.' Explain this statement with reference to the design of this chapter — its sources, its verse form, and its grammar of counsel.
questions.answer: The chapter shows three ways Sanskrit literature schools us in living. (1) Sources: it gathers its जीवनसंदेश from texts whose very purpose is guidance — the Bhagavadgita (a battlefield counsel on action and self-mastery), Bhartrhari's नीतिशतकम् (a hundred verses of worldly wisdom by a king turned poet), and anonymous subhashitas polished by centuries of recitation. (2) Form: each teaching is cast in metre, because a श्लोक is memorable — the lesson travels in the memory and surfaces exactly when life needs it, which plain prose rarely does. (3) Grammar: the verses speak in the विधिलिङ् (उद्धरेत्, त्यजेत्, भवेत्) — the optative mood of 'one should' — so the counsel is built into the verb itself: not a command barked at us, not a mere fact stated, but advice offered. Sources, metre and mood thus cooperate to make beauty carry wisdom.
questions.explanation: Three-part answer: sources of guidance, memorable verse form, and the optative as the mood of counsel.

questions.question: Write out from memory any two complete verses of this chapter (one from the Gita, one from Bhartrhari), name their sources, and state each verse's central message in one sentence.
questions.answer: Gita example: उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥ (Bhagavadgita 6.5) — message: lift yourself by your own self, for the disciplined self is your best friend and the undisciplined self your worst enemy. Bhartrhari example: केयूराणि न भूषयन्ति पुरुषं हारा न चन्द्रोज्ज्वलाः न स्नानं न विलेपनं न कुसुमं नालङ्कृता मूर्धजाः । वाण्येका समलङ्करोति पुरुषं या संस्कृता धार्यते क्षीयन्ते खलु भूषणानि सततं वाग्भूषणं भूषणम् ॥ (नीतिशतकम्) — message: cultivated speech, not perishable ornaments, is a person's one lasting adornment. (कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते... and विद्या नाम... equally acceptable.)
questions.explanation: Accurate quotation, correct attribution, one-line message for each.

questions.question: Write the full अन्वय of Bhartrhari's verse विद्या नाम नरस्य रूपमधिकं... and translate it clause by clause, explaining the function of नाम and the force of the closing विद्याविहीनः पशुः.
questions.answer: अन्वय: विद्या नाम नरस्य अधिकं रूपम्, प्रच्छन्नगुप्तं धनम् (च) । विद्या भोगकरी, यशःसुखकरी, गुरूणां गुरुः (च) । विदेशगमने विद्या बन्धुजनः, विद्या परा देवता । राजसु विद्या पूज्यते, न हि धनम् । विद्याविहीनः (नरः) पशुः । Clause-by-clause: Learning is truly a man's surpassing beauty and a hidden, guarded treasure; learning gives enjoyment, fame and happiness, and is the teacher of teachers; when one goes abroad learning is one's kinsman, learning is the highest deity; among kings it is learning, not wealth, that is honoured. नाम here is an emphatic particle — 'indeed/truly' — stamping the whole series of predicates as considered truth. The closing विद्याविहीनः पशुः is the verse's sting: strip a human of every excellence learning gives, and only animal existence remains — the strongest possible motivation to study.
questions.explanation: Full prose order, faithful translation, the emphatic नाम, and the climactic force of the last clause.

questions.question: Taking all six verses together, construct the chapter's single connected 'message of life' — show how self-reliance, desireless action, learning, speech, effort and austerity form one coherent programme for a young person.
questions.answer: The six verses interlock into one programme. Foundation: उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानम् — everything begins with self-reliance; no one else can lift you. Method of work: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते — act wholeheartedly but without anxiety for results, avoiding both greed and idleness. What to acquire: विद्या नाम... — direct that desireless effort above all toward learning, the one unstealable wealth that dignifies human life. How to carry it: वाग्भूषणम् — let your learning show in refined, kind speech, the only ornament that never wears out. The engine: यथा ह्येकेन चक्रेण — pair your effort with whatever destiny sends, since fate alone is a one-wheeled chariot. The price: सुखार्थिनः कुतो विद्या — accept that this path costs comfort; the student must renounce ease. Thus: rely on yourself, work without craving, aim at learning, express it in speech, drive with effort, and pay in austerity — a complete जीवनसंदेश.
questions.explanation: Synthesis question: the six morals must be woven into one ordered life-programme, not listed separately.

questions.question: Sandhi makes the verses of this chapter compact but hard to read. Taking कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन । मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि ॥ as your text, split the entire verse into its separate words and name every sandhi involved.
questions.answer: Word-split: कर्मणि + एव + अधिकारः + ते + मा + फलेषु + कदाचन । मा + कर्मफलहेतुः + भूः + मा + ते + सङ्गः + अस्तु + अकर्मणि ॥ Sandhis: (1) कर्मणि + एव = कर्मण्येव — यण्-सन्धिः (इ → य्). (2) एव + अधिकारः = एवाधिकारः — दीर्घ-सन्धिः (अ + अ = आ). (3) अधिकारः + ते = अधिकारस्ते — विसर्ग-सन्धिः (ः → स् before त्). (4) हेतुः + भूः = हेतुर्भूः and भूः + मा = भूर्मा — विसर्ग-सन्धिः (ः → र् before voiced sounds). (5) सङ्गः + अस्तु = सङ्गोऽस्तु — विसर्ग-सन्धिः with पूर्वरूपम् (अः + अ → ओ + ऽ). (6) अस्तु + अकर्मणि = अस्त्वकर्मणि — यण्-सन्धिः (उ → व्).
questions.explanation: One verse exercises yan, dirgha and three varieties of visarga sandhi.

questions.question: Analyse the following compounds from the chapter — कर्मफलहेतुः, विद्याविहीनः, वाग्भूषणम्, चन्द्रोज्ज्वलाः, विदेशगमनम् — giving for each the विग्रह, the समास type, and the meaning.
questions.answer: (1) कर्मफलहेतुः: कर्मणः फलं कर्मफलम्; कर्मफलं हेतुः यस्य सः — बहुव्रीहिः (built on an inner षष्ठी-तत्पुरुष); 'one whose motive is the fruit of action'. (2) विद्याविहीनः: विद्यया विहीनः — तृतीया-तत्पुरुषः; 'devoid of learning'. (3) वाग्भूषणम्: वाचः भूषणम् — षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः (with जश्त्व sandhi वाक् → वाग्); 'the ornament of speech'. (4) चन्द्रोज्ज्वलाः: चन्द्रः इव उज्ज्वलाः — उपमानपूर्वपद (कर्मधारय) compound; 'bright like the moon', describing necklaces. (5) विदेशगमनम्: विदेशं गमनम् — द्वितीया-तत्पुरुषः; 'going abroad', used in the locative विदेशगमने 'when one goes abroad'.
questions.explanation: Five compounds spanning bahuvrihi, three tatpurusha varieties and an upamana compound.

questions.question: Survey the verb system of the chapter's verses: classify every finite verb form under विधिलिङ्, लट् (कर्तरि), कर्मणि प्रयोग, and निषेध with मा, and explain what each construction contributes to the verses' meaning.
questions.answer: विधिलिङ् (counsel, 'should'): उद्धरेत्, अवसादयेत् (causative, with न), भवेत्, त्यजेत् (twice) — these voice the chapter's advice. लट् कर्तरि (present statements of fact): भूषयन्ति ('do not adorn', with न), समलङ्करोति ('truly adorns'), सिध्यति ('does not succeed', with न), क्षीयन्ते ('wear away') — these state the timeless facts on which the advice rests. कर्मणि प्रयोग (passive): पूज्यते ('is honoured'), धार्यते ('is borne') — the passive foregrounds विद्या and वाणी as the honoured/maintained things rather than any particular agent. निषेध with मा (prohibition): मा भूः ('do not become'), मा अस्तु ('let there not be') — Sanskrit uses मा, not न, for prohibitions; these two forms carry the Gita's double warning. Together: facts in लट्, honours in the passive, warnings with मा, and counsel in the optative — the verb system itself maps the rhetoric of the verses.
questions.explanation: Complete inventory plus the rhetorical function of each construction.

questions.question: Prepare a short bilingual 'message of life' for your school magazine: choose any three verses of this chapter, translate each into polished English, and add for each two sentences on why it speaks to students today. Conclude with one Sanskrit sentence of your own composition.
questions.answer: Model answer: (1) उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानम् — 'Raise yourself by your own self; never let yourself sink: the self alone is your friend, the self alone your foe.' In an age of comparison and social media, this verse relocates both the problem and the power within us; discipline of one's own mind outweighs every external circumstance. (2) कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते — 'Your right is to the work alone, never to its fruits.' Exam anxiety is fruit-anxiety; this verse frees the student to pour everything into preparation while holding results lightly, and it equally forbids the escape of giving up. (3) वाग्भूषणं भूषणम् — 'Ornaments all wear away; cultivated speech is the ornament forever.' Brands and gadgets date quickly, but the way we speak — precise, truthful, kind — adorns us in every interview and friendship for life. Concluding Sanskrit sentence (example): वयम् उद्यमेन विद्यां सेवेमहि, संस्कृतया वाण्या च जीवेम । (May we serve learning with effort, and live with cultivated speech.) Any coherent selection, faithful translations and a correct concluding sentence merit full marks.
questions.explanation: Open composition task: selection, translation quality, present-day relevance, and one original Sanskrit sentence.

questions.question: Read the verse and answer: उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥ (a) Give the शब्दार्थ of उद्धरेत् and अवसादयेत्. (b) Which word occurs in three different case-forms in the verse? Name the forms.
questions.answer: (a) उद्धरेत् = 'one should lift up/raise'; अवसादयेत् = 'one should (not) let sink / cause to sink' (causative). (b) The word आत्मन् occurs as आत्मना (तृतीया, 'by the self'), आत्मानम् (द्वितीया, 'the self' as object), आत्मा (प्रथमा, 'the self' as subject) and आत्मनः (षष्ठी, 'of the self') — any three of these four forms earn the marks.
questions.explanation: The verse is a virtual declension drill on आत्मन्.

questions.question: Read: सुखार्थिनः कुतो विद्या कुतो विद्यार्थिनः सुखम् । सुखार्थी वा त्यजेद्विद्यां विद्यार्थी वा त्यजेत्सुखम् ॥ (a) Write the अन्वय of the first line. (b) What is the difference in विभक्ति between सुखार्थिनः (line 1) and सुखार्थी (line 2), and why does it change?
questions.answer: (a) अन्वय: सुखार्थिनः विद्या कुतः? विद्यार्थिनः सुखं कुतः? (For the comfort-seeker, whence learning? For the learning-seeker, whence comfort?) (b) In line 1 सुखार्थिनः is षष्ठी एकवचन ('of/for the comfort-seeker' — possessor of the impossible learning); in line 2 सुखार्थी is प्रथमा एकवचन, because there it is the subject of the verb त्यजेत् ('let the comfort-seeker give up...'). The role changes from possessor to agent, so the case changes.
questions.explanation: Same stem अर्थिन्, two cases: genitive of relation vs nominative subject.

questions.question: Situation: Riya studies sincerely all year but before results she cannot sleep, and after one poor mark-sheet she declares she will stop studying since 'marks are all luck anyway'. Which TWO teachings of Gita 2.47 has she violated, and what would the verse advise her?
questions.answer: She violates both prohibitions. First, her sleepless obsession with results makes her कर्मफलहेतुः — one whose motive and mind are fixed on the fruit (मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूः). Second, her decision to stop studying is सङ्गः अकर्मणि — attachment to inaction (मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि). The verse's advice: her अधिकार is over the studying itself — steady, wholehearted work — while results must be left to take care of themselves; neither anxiety nor abandonment of effort is the way.
questions.explanation: The case embodies both forbidden extremes of the verse.

questions.question: Situation: Arjun moves alone to a new city for college. He knows nobody, feels friendless, and messages home that 'everything here is against me'. His grandmother replies with two lines: विद्या बन्धुजनो विदेशगमने and आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुः. Explain what each quotation offers Arjun and how the two together answer his complaint.
questions.answer: The first line (Bhartrhari) tells Arjun that in a strange place his learning itself is his kinsman — his knowledge and skills will win him respect, opportunities and eventually friends; he has not arrived empty-handed. The second (Gita 6.5) tells him the decisive friend is his own self: a disciplined, positive mind will befriend him in the friendless city, while self-pity would be the real enemy 'against' him. Together they answer his complaint by relocating support from outside to within: he already carries both companions — his विद्या and his own mastered आत्मा — so nothing external is truly 'against' him.
questions.explanation: Application of two verses to one situation: learning as kinsman, self as friend.

questions.question: Situation: Two friends argue. Meera: 'Success is written in destiny; toppers are just lucky.' Kavya: 'Luck is irrelevant; effort alone decides everything.' Using यथा ह्येकेन चक्रेण न रथस्य गतिर्भवेत् । एवं पुरुषकारेण विना दैवं न सिध्यति ॥ judge BOTH positions and state the verse's own view.
questions.answer: The verse rejects both extremes. Against Meera: destiny alone is a one-wheeled chariot — दैवं without पुरुषकार does not succeed (न सिध्यति), so waiting on luck guarantees standstill. Against Kavya the verse offers a partial correction: it does not deny दैव's existence — it keeps destiny as one wheel — it only insists that destiny bears fruit through effort. The verse's own view is complementarity: circumstances (दैव) and self-exertion (पुरुषकार) are the chariot's two wheels; a wise student accepts what circumstances give and supplies the second wheel of maximum effort, since that is the only wheel in her hands.
questions.explanation: Evaluation of two one-wheeled positions against the verse's two-wheel doctrine.

questions.question: A student transcribing the Gita writes: 'कर्मणि एव अधिकारः ते मा फलेषु कदाचन' — all words separate. (a) Join the first four words with correct sandhi as in the original verse. (b) Name the two sandhis you applied.
questions.answer: (a) कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते (कर्मणि + एव → कर्मण्येव; एव + अधिकारः → एवाधिकारः; अधिकारः + ते → अधिकारस्ते). (b) यण्-सन्धिः (इ → य् in कर्मण्येव), दीर्घ-सन्धिः (अ + अ = आ in एवाधिकारः) and विसर्ग-सन्धिः (ः → स् in अधिकारस्ते) — any correctly named two of these three earn the naming marks.
questions.explanation: Reverse exercise: applying sandhi rather than splitting it.

questions.question: Read: वाण्येका समलङ्करोति पुरुषं या संस्कृता धार्यते । क्षीयन्ते खलु भूषणानि सततं वाग्भूषणं भूषणम् ॥ (a) Split वाण्येका and name the sandhi. (b) वाग्भूषणम् contains both a sandhi and a samasa — identify each. (c) Why is the क् of वाक् not retained unchanged?
questions.answer: (a) वाण्येका = वाणी + एका — यण्-सन्धिः (ई → य् before ए). (b) Sandhi: वाक् + भूषणम् = वाग्भूषणम्, जश्त्व (व्यञ्जन-सन्धि); samasa: वाचः भूषणम् — षष्ठी-तत्पुरुषः, 'ornament of speech'. (c) The voiceless क् cannot stand before the voiced भ्; by the जश्त्व rule it assimilates in voicing and becomes ग्.
questions.explanation: One compound word exhibiting consonant sandhi wrapped around a genitive tatpurusha.

questions.question: Read: विद्या नाम नरस्य रूपमधिकं प्रच्छन्नगुप्तं धनं ... विद्या राजसु पूज्यते न हि धनम् । (a) State the विभक्ति and role of नरस्य and राजसु. (b) The word धनम् appears twice — as what part of the sentence each time? (c) Analyse प्रच्छन्नगुप्तम् as a compound of two participles.
questions.answer: (a) नरस्य = षष्ठी एकवचन, 'of a man' (possession); राजसु = सप्तमी बहुवचन, 'among kings' (locative sphere). (b) First धनम् is a predicate nominative — विद्या IS (a hidden) treasure; second धनम् is the negated subject of पूज्यते understood — 'wealth is NOT honoured' (न हि धनम् [पूज्यते]). (c) प्रच्छन्नगुप्तम् = प्रच्छन्नं च गुप्तं च — two क्त-participles (प्र+छद्, गुप्) conjoined (कर्मधारय/द्वन्द्व-like pairing) qualifying धनम्: 'hidden and guarded'.
questions.explanation: Case roles, ellipsis of the repeated verb, and a double-participle compound.

questions.question: Read: क्षीयन्ते खलु भूषणानि सततं वाग्भूषणं भूषणम् । and विद्या राजसु पूज्यते । (a) Parse क्षीयन्ते and पूज्यते: root, लकार/voice, person, number. (b) The clause वाग्भूषणं भूषणम् has no verb — what verb is understood, and what is this sentence type called?
questions.answer: (a) क्षीयन्ते: root क्षि 'to decay', लट् लकार, आत्मनेपद/passive-type -य- present, third person plural — '(ornaments) wear away'. पूज्यते: root पूज् 'to honour', लट् लकार, कर्मणि प्रयोग (passive), third person singular — '(learning) is honoured'. (b) The verb अस्ति ('is') is understood: वाग्भूषणं (सततं) भूषणम् (अस्ति). A sentence with an omitted copula is a nominal sentence — common in Sanskrit maxims, e.g. विद्याविहीनः पशुः.
questions.explanation: Verb parsing plus recognition of the copula-less nominal sentence.

questions.question: Three students translate सततं वाग्भूषणं भूषणम्: (A) 'The ornament of speech is always an ornament.' (B) 'Speech is the one ornament that never fades.' (C) 'Always wear the jewellery called speech.' Rank the three translations, justifying your ranking on accuracy and idiom, and give your own best rendering.
questions.answer: Ranking: B, A, C. (B) is best: it is idiomatic and captures the verse's point — permanence (सततम्) and exclusivity (एका earlier in the verse) — though it renders सततम् as 'never fades' rather than literally 'always'. (A) is literally faithful (वाग्भूषणम् = ornament of speech; सततम् = always) but flat English: 'is always an ornament' blunts the contrast with क्षीयन्ते भूषणानि. (C) is worst: 'wear the jewellery' invents an imperative the verse does not have and turns a declaration into advice about accessories, losing the metaphor's direction. Own rendering (example): 'All ornaments wear away; refined speech alone adorns forever.' Any rendering preserving permanence, exclusivity and the declarative form is acceptable.
questions.explanation: Evaluation of translation trade-offs: literal accuracy vs idiom vs outright distortion.
